whoIsThisFor.heading: Who is the Field Service Consultant exam for?

personas.label: Service Cloud consultants expanding scope
personas.description: You already implement Service Cloud and want to add Field Service expertise for mobile workforce management projects.

personas.label: Field operations managers
personas.description: You manage dispatchers and field technicians using Salesforce Field Service and want to validate your configuration and scheduling knowledge.

personas.label: Implementation partners
personas.description: You deliver Field Service implementations for clients and need the consultant credential to demonstrate end-to-end solution design expertise.

examDifficulty.heading: How to Prepare for the Exam
examDifficulty.summary: The official outline assigns the largest weight to Managing Scheduling and Optimization (28%) and Managing Work Orders (23%). Use the published domains to plan a balanced review.
bullets: Exam format: 60 multiple-choice/multiple-select questions and up to five unscored questions in 105 minutes.
Passing score: 63%; No pass-rate figure is stated in the exam guide reviewed.
Prerequisites: Salesforce Certified Platform Administrator and Salesforce Certified Agentforce Service Consultant.
Exam objectives: scheduling and optimization, work orders, resources, mobility, inventory, assets, maintenance plans, and permissions/sharing.
examDifficulty.passRateGuidance: Use practice questions diagnostically, then verify concepts against the official exam outline and Salesforce Help. Practice scores are not an official threshold or a guarantee of exam results.

examFormat.heading: Exam Format and Study Approach
examFormat.intro: The Salesforce exam guide specifies 60 scored multiple-choice/multiple-select questions, up to five unscored questions, and 105 minutes. The registration fee is US$200 plus applicable taxes; retake fee is US$100 plus applicable taxes.
bestWayToPass: Read each scenario for the business requirement, affected record, current lifecycle state, and constraints before selecting a configuration.
Separate resource qualification (skills and territory membership) from scheduling objectives (the desired outcome among eligible choices).
Trace work from Work Order and Work Order Line Items to associated Service Appointments; distinguish planned products from consumed products.
Compare scheduling-service and optimization-service choices only after identifying scope, timing, and dispatch requirements.
Review every published exam domain, including mobility, assets, maintenance plans, and permissions/sharing.

certificationCard.code: Agentforce Field Service and Operations Consultant
certificationCard.description: The Salesforce Certified Agentforce Field Service and Operations Consultant credential validates the ability to design and deploy Field Service and Operations solutions for customer business processes.

keyConcepts.h2: Field Service Consultant: Key Concepts for the Exam

blocks.heading: Field Service Objects: Work Orders, Appointments, and Resources
blocks.body: The Field Service data model centres on **Work Orders** (the service job), **Work Order Line Items** (specific tasks within the job), **Service Appointments** (the scheduled visit), and **Service Resources** (the worker, equipment, or crew). Assets track the customer equipment being serviced. Locations store physical addresses for service territories and parts inventory. The consultant must understand how these objects relate and how data flows from a Case → Work Order → Service Appointment → Resource assignment and completion.

blocks.heading: Scheduling and the Gantt
blocks.body: The **Dispatcher Console** **Gantt** view shows all appointments on a timeline by resource. Drag-and-drop scheduling assigns appointments to resources. The Scheduling Policy defines the rules for the scheduler — constraints (working hours, required skills, territory) and objectives (minimise travel, maximise utilisation). Appointment Booking lets customers or agents select available slots. The In-Day Optimisation automatically reschedules appointments as the day changes (cancellations, new high-priority jobs). Know the difference between manual scheduling and automated optimisation.

blocks.heading: Service Territories, Resources, and Skills
blocks.body: Service Territories define the geographic areas where resources operate — Primary territory (where the resource primarily works) and Secondary/Relocation territories for expanded coverage. Service Resources are linked to Salesforce users (Employee type) or equipment (Equipment type). Skills define the competencies required for a Work Order — resources must have matching skills for skills-based routing. Operating Hours define when territories and resources are available. For a routing scenario, check the resource’s active territory membership, required skills and skill levels, and applicable operating hours.

blocks.heading: Mobile App and Offline Capabilities
blocks.body: Field Service Mobile supports technician workflows on mobile devices; available records and behavior depend on configured mobile settings and data access. When assessing an offline requirement, distinguish the mobile app capability from the specific data, actions, and sync configuration available to the user. Do not assume every record or flow is available offline.

blocks.heading: Parts and Inventory Management
blocks.body: Products Required list the parts needed for a Work Order before the job. Products Consumed record actual parts used during the service visit. Return Orders handle parts returned to inventory. Locations track physical inventory (van stock, warehouse, customer site). Inventory transfers move stock between locations. The Service Report summarises the completed work, parts used, and technician notes — can be auto-generated and sent to the customer upon job completion. Know the difference between Products Required (planned) and Products Consumed (actual).

scenarioTips.intro: These original examples are study aids, not reported exam items. Use official documentation to confirm product behavior and local configuration details.

blocks.heading: Resource eligibility versus preference
blocks.body: A job is in a service territory but the expected technician is not considered. Check active Service Territory Members, required skills and skill levels, and operating hours before treating an account or Work Order resource preference as a hard eligibility rule.

blocks.heading: Appointment lifecycle versus schedule policy
blocks.body: A dispatcher cannot schedule an appointment with the expected policy. First check the appointment status, required fields, and whether the selected scheduling service supports the requested operation. A policy objective cannot repair an invalid lifecycle state.

blocks.heading: Planned versus actual parts
blocks.body: A Work Order lists parts expected before dispatch, but the technician uses a different quantity. Distinguish Products Required from Products Consumed; then verify the relevant inventory location and whether returned parts require a Return Order.

sampleQuestions.question: Which record represents a technician or other worker that can be assigned field service work?
sampleQuestions.explanation: A Service Resource represents a person or other resource used in field operations. Availability is affected by related configuration and is not simply a property of the record alone.
whyWrong: Service Appointment represents scheduled work, not technician availability itself.
Service Territory defines a geographic/logical area, not individual technician availability.
Operating Hours define when a resource/location is generally open, but Service Resource specifically represents the technician's availability record.

sampleQuestions.question: What is the purpose of a Scheduling Policy in Field Service?
options: To define work rules and objectives for the optimizer
sampleQuestions.explanation: Scheduling Policies define work rules (constraints) and objectives that the scheduling optimizer uses when assigning appointments.
whyWrong: Assigning resources to territories is a separate configuration, not what a Scheduling Policy defines.
Tracking service appointments is a record-management function, not what a Scheduling Policy defines.
Managing parts inventory is a separate Field Service function, unrelated to Scheduling Policy's optimizer rules.

sampleQuestions.question: Which feature allows field technicians to access their schedule and update work orders offline?
sampleQuestions.explanation: The Field Service Mobile App allows technicians to access schedules, update work orders, and capture signatures even without internet connectivity.
whyWrong: Service Console is a general Salesforce interface, not the mobile offline-capable app for technicians.
Lightning Experience is the general desktop interface, not the mobile offline app for field technicians.
Dispatcher Console is used by dispatchers in the office, not by field technicians in the field.

sampleQuestions.question: What determines which technicians are eligible to be scheduled for a service appointment?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Skill Requirements on the Work Type and Service Territory membership determine which Service Resources are eligible for scheduling.
whyWrong: User Profile alone controls broad access, not the specific scheduling eligibility criteria.
Permission Sets grant feature access, not specifically scheduling eligibility.
Role Hierarchy determines record visibility, not specifically technician scheduling eligibility.

sampleQuestions.question: Which component shows dispatchers a visual timeline of scheduled appointments?
sampleQuestions.explanation: The Dispatcher Console Gantt shows a visual timeline of scheduled appointments across service resources.
whyWrong: Calendar View shows a different, less operationally detailed schedule view.
List View shows tabular data, not the visual timeline dispatchers use.
Map View shows geographic location, not the visual scheduling timeline being described.

sampleQuestions.question: What is the purpose of Work Type in Field Service?
options: To define the template for work orders including duration, skills, and parts
sampleQuestions.explanation: Work Type defines the template for work orders including duration and skill requirements.
whyWrong: 'To track inventory only' misattributes Work Type's purpose to a different Field Service function.
Assigning territories is a separate configuration, unrelated to Work Type's template purpose.
Creating reports is a separate function, unrelated to Work Type's template purpose.

sampleQuestions.question: Which object links a Service Appointment to a Work Order?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Service Appointments are child records of Work Orders.
whyWrong: Service Resource represents the technician, not the object linking appointment to work order.
Operating Hours define availability windows, not the appointment-to-work-order link.
Service Territory defines a geographic area, not the appointment-to-work-order link.

sampleQuestions.question: What does the scheduling optimizer consider when assigning appointments?
options: Skills, availability, travel time, and scheduling policies
sampleQuestions.explanation: The optimizer considers skills, availability, travel, and policies.
whyWrong: 'Only territory' undersells the optimizer's broader consideration of skills, travel time, and policies.
'Only skills' undersells the optimizer's broader consideration of availability, travel time, and policies.
'Only travel time' undersells the optimizer's broader consideration of skills, availability, and policies.

sampleQuestions.question: Which feature allows dispatchers to manually drag and drop appointments?
sampleQuestions.explanation: The Gantt allows manual drag-and-drop scheduling.
whyWrong: List View alone doesn't support drag-and-drop scheduling — that's the Gantt's specific function.
Map View alone doesn't support drag-and-drop scheduling — that's the Gantt's specific function.
Reports display data — they don't support interactive drag-and-drop scheduling.

sampleQuestions.question: What is the purpose of Operating Hours in Field Service?
options: To define when resources and locations are available
sampleQuestions.explanation: Operating Hours define availability windows for resources and locations.
whyWrong: 'To define skills only' undersells Operating Hours, which is about availability windows, not skills.
'To track parts only' misattributes Operating Hours' purpose to a different Field Service function.
'To create work orders' misattributes Operating Hours' purpose to a different Field Service function.

sampleQuestions.question: Which object is used to track consumable or returnable parts for work orders?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Product Required and Product Consumed track parts on work orders.
whyWrong: Service Resource represents the technician, not the parts-tracking object.
Work Type defines the job template, not the specific parts-tracking object.
Service Territory defines a geographic area, unrelated to tracking parts.

sampleQuestions.question: What does the Field Service Mobile app support for technicians?
options: Offline access, capture signatures, and photo attachments
sampleQuestions.explanation: The mobile app supports offline work, signatures, and photos.
whyWrong: 'Online only' is the opposite of what the mobile app's offline capability provides.
'Reports only' undersells the mobile app's broader field capabilities (offline, signatures, photos).
'Dashboards only' undersells the mobile app's broader field capabilities (offline, signatures, photos).

sampleQuestions.question: Which feature enables automatic scheduling based on optimization rules?
sampleQuestions.explanation: The optimization service runs with scheduling policies for automatic assignment.
whyWrong: Manual assignment is the opposite of the automated optimization being asked about.
Gantt alone is a visualization tool, not the automated scheduling engine itself.
Map View alone is a visualization tool, not the automated scheduling engine itself.

sampleQuestions.question: What is a Service Territory used for?
options: To define geographic or logical areas for resource assignment
sampleQuestions.explanation: Service Territories define areas for resource assignment and routing.
whyWrong: 'To track parts only' misattributes Service Territory's purpose to a different Field Service function.
'To create work types only' misattributes Service Territory's purpose to a different Field Service function.
'To manage contracts only' misattributes Service Territory's purpose to a different Field Service function.

sampleQuestions.question: Which Field Service feature supports contract-based entitlements and SLAs?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Service Contracts and Entitlements define SLAs and covered services.
whyWrong: Work Type alone defines job templates, not entitlement/SLA tracking.
Operating Hours alone define availability windows, not entitlement/SLA tracking.
Service Resource alone represents technicians, not entitlement/SLA tracking.
